Join a Split "MC" Surname Prefix

Source: R/prep_name.R
join_mc.Rd

Inside a name, a standalone MC starts a surname written with a space (STEVE MC CORMICK, DENISE MC DERMOTT). It is joined to the next word without a dash (MCCORMICK), the spelling the census lists and other records use. A leading MC before two or more words is joined to the next word with a dash (MC NELLY TORRES -> MC-NELLY); before one word it is left as initials (MC OLSON). A trailing MC is a credential (Navy Medical Corps) and is left for the title rules, as is an MC followed by a credential or suffix (SANFORD MC USN) or by a word starting with MC.

Usage

join_mc(x)

Arguments

x

A character vector of upper-cased, space-separated names.

Value

x with split MC surnames joined.

Details

(This replaces a rule that cut everything after a standalone MC, which turned CHARLES MC SPADDEN into CHARLES MC.)
